summary: Commissions and grows a mixed portfolio of skills and experiential opportunities beyond the course, combining reusable evergreen provision, short active experiences and sustained intensive opportunities to increase both student reach and depth over time.
detailSummary:
This deliverable provides the commissioning mechanism through which King’s Edge turns identified need into funded student opportunity beyond the course. It brings together requirements emerging from across the programme and converts them into a balanced portfolio of scalable evergreen, short active and sustained intensive provision, allowing investment to be distributed deliberately across reach, depth and strategic value.

In Year 1, a £150,000 commissioning portfolio will support four year-round programmes focused on final-year career enhancement, entrepreneurship and enterprise, belonging and connection, and service and community-engaged experience. Together, these will engage at least 2,500 distinct students, around 6% of the current King’s student population, in substantive beyond-course opportunities. Package-level planning anticipates approximately 26,500 to 33,500 student-hours and around 350 sustained high-intensity places.

The portfolio uses three complementary delivery modes. Scalable evergreen opportunities create reusable entry points, including skills courses, self-directed provision and repeatable projects, that can reach increasing numbers of students at relatively low marginal cost. Short active experiences turn that reach into meaningful participation through challenges, workshops, sprints, sandpits and other formats in which students practise, make or contribute. Sustained intensive opportunities provide the deepest forms of experiential learning through projects, placements, mentoring and comparable longer experiences. This high-touch layer is deliberately capacity-limited and grows to a viable plateau rather than being expected to scale indefinitely.

The three-year mobilisation model uses annual investment of £150,000 in Year 1, £200,000 in Year 2 and £250,000 in Year 3 to build both annual opportunity supply and an accumulating reusable asset base. The working ambition is for distinct student reach to grow from at least 2,500 in Year 1 to 4,000 in Year 2 and 6,500 in Year 3, while student-hours rise more steeply from approximately 26,500 to 33,500, to 55,000 to 65,000, and then 100,000 to 115,000. Sustained high-intensity places grow from around 350 to around 500 and then around 600.

At steady state, an indicative £175,000 annual business-as-usual investment sustains and refreshes the accumulated portfolio rather than recreating it from scratch. The working ambition is to reach around 9,000 distinct students each year, approximately 20% of the current King’s student population, while generating around 145,000 to 165,000 student-hours and protecting around 600 sustained high-intensity places. The lower annual cash requirement is made possible by continued use of evergreen assets created during mobilisation, with recurring investment focused on refresh, facilitation, responsive commissioning and the people-intensive forms of experience that cannot scale in the same way.

Early commissioning will respond to known priorities and concrete gaps in the student experience, including graduate futures, entrepreneurship, service and community engagement, belonging and participation. Over time, the portfolio will become increasingly informed by external and future-facing insight, the experiential learning North Star and, as King’s Canvas matures, richer evidence about student purpose and demand. Commissioned provision should give students something meaningful to practise, contribute, produce or carry forward. Alongside curriculum-embedded opportunity growth through 2.1.4, this gives King’s Edge a direct mechanism for creating additional supply where existing provision is insufficient or uneven.
problemSolved: King’s lacks a coherent mechanism for turning identified student need, strategic priorities and evidence about future relevance into funded beyond-course provision at scale. As a result, opportunity supply is uneven, gaps can persist, and access to meaningful skills and experience can depend too heavily on local capacity, historic provision or student confidence and networks.
whatChanges: King’s Edge establishes a standing commissioning portfolio that converts identified need into funded, substantive beyond-course opportunities and deliberately balances reach and depth. A three-year mobilisation investment of £150,000, £200,000 and £250,000 progressively builds reusable evergreen provision, short active opportunities and sustained intensive capacity, growing distinct student reach from at least 2,500 to 4,000 and then 6,500 while student-hours grow faster. At steady state, an indicative £175,000 annual investment sustains and refreshes this accumulated asset base, with an ambition to reach around 9,000 students, approximately 20% of the current King’s student population, while maintaining around 600 sustained high-intensity places.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s has a rich but uneven ecology of opportunities beyond the curriculum, but it does not yet have a coherent mechanism for turning evidence about student need, strategic priorities and future relevance into funded provision at scale.

Different parts of King’s can identify gaps, emerging needs and valuable forms of experience, but these do not consistently translate into a coordinated portfolio of opportunities for students. Provision can depend on local capacity, historic activity or individual initiative, with limited ability to balance reach, depth, access and strategic value across the institution.

Without a deliberate commissioning route, King’s Edge risks becoming better at understanding what students need and helping them navigate what already exists, without creating enough new supply where meaningful gaps remain.
caseForChange.opportunity:
King’s can establish a standing commissioning capability that converts emerging requirements from across King’s Edge into a balanced portfolio of substantive skills and experiential opportunities beyond the course.

Investment can be directed across three complementary modes: reusable evergreen provision that creates scalable entry points, short active experiences that turn reach into meaningful participation, and sustained intensive opportunities that protect depth. By accumulating high-quality evergreen courses and projects over successive years, the portfolio can increase student reach and student-hours faster than annual expenditure while continuing to protect the people-intensive experiences that cannot scale in the same way.

Over time, commissioning can become increasingly informed by student purpose and demand, external and future-facing insight, participation needs and the developing experiential learning North Star. This gives King’s a practical mechanism for growing provision where evidence suggests it will add most value.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is moving from proposition into mobilisation. Several parts of the programme are beginning to create concrete requirements for new opportunities beyond the curriculum, while richer sources of demand intelligence will come online progressively rather than all at once.

There is therefore a need to begin commissioning now against clear early priorities, while building a model capable of becoming more evidence-led as external validation, the experiential learning framework and King’s Canvas mature.

The immediate graduate futures context also creates a strong case for action. Students need access to substantive skills and experiences that strengthen their ability to move into the futures they want, particularly where existing graduate pathways or access to opportunity are less assured.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s develops a repeatable way of turning student need, strategic priorities and evidence about future relevance into funded opportunities beyond the course.

A managed portfolio of reusable evergreen, short active and sustained intensive provision gives students access to meaningful skills development and experience, with investment deliberately balanced across reach and depth. Successive mobilisation years build both annual opportunity supply and an accumulating asset base, allowing more students to participate and total student-hours to grow faster than annual expenditure. Sustained intensive capacity grows to a viable level and is then protected as the high-touch layer of the portfolio.

At business-as-usual steady state, recurring investment sustains, refreshes and selectively expands the portfolio rather than recreating it from scratch. Alongside curriculum-embedded opportunity growth through 2.1.4, this gives King’s Edge a direct mechanism for creating the additional experiences students need rather than relying only on existing provision.
